name: Seminoe State Park (South Red Hills Campground)
note: South Red Hills is the campground just south of North Red Hills on the northwest side of Seminoe Reservoir, about 34 mi north of Sinclair via County Road 351: two clusters of gravel sites, several with shade shelters, on open sage slopes above the water beside the South Red Hills boat ramp. No trees. The park's dump station is at North Red Hills. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 14 'Seminoe State Park', FacilityId 382 'South Red Hills', read 2026-11-20): 21 web-bookable units - 20 'Campsite Non-Electric' SR42-SR61 (IsRVSite true, 'Unit&parkingsize' 40 on every unit, gravel pads, 7 pull-throughs) + Group Site SR41 -> real drive-in RV campground a 23-ft rig fits. The Dyrt (South Red Hills Area, read 2026-11-20): 21 campsites, 'RV access up to 40 feet', $10/night. Not in the DB: the only entry within 2 km is 6360 North Red Hills (FacilityId 381), 0.8 km NE, a separate facility; no name match. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery at 42.1310,-106.8990 (660 m frame) and 260 m / 220 m frames over the east, west and NE parts, every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 382) plotted; images rendered. Full pool 6,357.0 ft NGVD29 (Reclamation allocation table) = 1938.7 m NAVD88 (NOAA NCAT/VERTCON at the site); USGS 3DEP lidar (epqs.nationalmap.gov) water surface 1932.0 m. Profiles from the pads to the full-pool contour: SR42 (pull-through with shelter at the end of the north road, ~42.13228,-106.89579; pad ~1941.7 m) - flat 4 m, then a ~2.8 m bank (1941.5 -> 1938.7 in 4 m) to the full-pool line ~8 m off, open bare drawdown ground to the imaged water ~25-30 m off; SR43 - full-pool line ~18 m S down a ~30-degree bank (1943.1 -> 1937.5 in 10 m) or ~62 m E on gentle ground; SR45 ~78 m; SR46 ~43 m down a 13 m drop (~29% sage slope); SR58 ~45 m, SR59 ~25-40 m and SR60 ~10-15 m above the sand floor of a dry cove (cove floor 1935-1936 m, so it floods only near full pool), 4-6 m down a slope. Every campsite is tagged 'Waterfront Setting: None' by the booking engine (only the group site SR41 is tagged 'Reservoir'). Nearest candidate SR42 sits on a bank ~3 m above full pool; SR59/SR60 front a cove that is dry sand below full pool -> no RV pad clearly on open ground at the water's edge: downgraded to lakeview. View floor: the pads sit on open sage slopes with the reservoir unscreened below.

fees.note: $10 a night for Wyoming residents, $18 for others, plus the day-use fee, $7 a vehicle for residents and $12 for others, plus sales and lodging tax. The booking site shows 'Fees Range From $23-41' on the campsites.

facilities_source: Search-result text of the park's own pages (https://wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/activities-amenities-seminoe/restroom-facilities-seminoe and .../campsites-for-rvs-seminoe; the site itself not fetched, F5 challenge), read 2026-11-20: ten vault toilets throughout the park, restrooms open all year; 'water can be obtained in the North Red Hills and South Red Hills during the summer months'. Campflare (FacilityId 382 page, read 2026-11-20): 'Vault toilets are available year-round, and potable water spigots operate during the summer season.' season.note: Off season (Sep 16 - May 14) the sites are walk-up, paid at the entrance fee kiosks.

booking.note: Reservations required May 15 - Sep 15; off season the sites are walk-up.

booking_source: reserve.wyoming.gov US eDirect API FacilityId 382: AllowWebBooking true on all 21 units; Restrictions MinimumStay 1, MaximumStay 14; in-season 2027-05-15..2027-09-15 (IsWalkin on off-season nights), read 2026-11-20 + the park page capture 2026-10-12 ('Campsite reservations required from May 15th through September 15th'). The Dyrt's 'May 1-September 30' busy season disagrees with both.
flags: Waterfront downgraded to lakeview: SR42 (end of the north road) sits ~3 m above full pool with the full-pool line ~8 m off down a short bank and open drawdown ground to the water beyond - the reviewer may judge it a single lakefront site with a caveat; the engine tags it 'Waterfront Setting: None'. SR59/SR60 front a dry sand cove that holds water only near full pool. Pad positions tie to engine MapInfo points, which looked offset by up to ~25 m at SR42.
